'''Alan James Southward''' (17 April 1928 – 27 October 2007) was a British [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] who studied [[Marine ecosystem|marine ecology]], [[Barnacle|barnacles]], [[Siboglinidae|tube worms]], and deep-sea [[Hydrothermal vent|hydrothermal vents]]. Southward was born and raised in [[Liverpool]], England. He studied at the [[University of Liverpool]]. His PhD, obtained for that school in 1951, was on the ecology of the [[Intertidal zone|foreshore]] of the [[Isle of Man]]. Southward was a "world expert on the taxonomy of barnacles" and wrote two books on them, but was also interested in the ecology of hydrothermal vents, which he studied with his wife, [[Eve Southward]]. He retired in 1987 but continued to work and publish in the field of marine biology until his death in 2007.

== Life and education ==
Southward was born on 17 April 1928 in [[Liverpool]], England. His father worked for [[Cunard Line|Cunard]] engineering as a [[shipfitter]]. As a teenager, Southward attended [[Liverpool Collegiate School]]. A [[meningitis]] infection around that time{{Efn|Sources differ on whether he was 14<ref name="Chris Fry"/> or 15.<ref name="Steve Hawkins"/>}} left him deaf. He went on to study at the [[University of Liverpool]]; in 1948 (age 20) he earned [[first-class honours]] for his zoology work. He obtained a PhD in 1951, working at a biological station on the [[Isle of Man]].<ref name="Times Obit">{{Cite web |date=2007-11-29 |title=Professor Alan Southward |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-alan-southward-cf7k8rlw0pd |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="Steve Hawkins">{{Cite news |last=Hawkins |first=Steve |date=2007-11-17 |title=Alan Southward |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/nov/17/guardianobituaries.obituaries |access-date=2026-03-15 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name="Paul R. Dando">{{Cite journal |last=Dando |first=Paul R. |date=3 Jan 2008 |title=Alan J. Southward (1928–2007) |url=https://archive.org/details/NatureMagazine7174-2008-01-03/page/28/mode/2up?q=%22Alan+J.+Southward+%281928%E2%80%932007%29%22 |journal=[[Nature Magazine]] |volume=451 |issue=7174 |page=28 |doi=10.1038/451028a |pmid=18172490 }}</ref><ref name="Chris Fry">{{Cite journal |last=Fry |first=Chris |date=1 Feb 2008 |title=Professor Alan Southward CBiol FlBiol |journal=Biologist |volume=55 |issue=1 |page=47}}</ref> His thesis, the result of three years of field work, was titled ''On the Ecology of the Foreshore of the South of the Isle of Man''.<ref>{{Cite web |title='On the Ecology of the Foreshore of the South of the Isle of Man' |url=https://www.imuseum.im/search/archive_record/view?id=mnh-museum-672364 |website=imuseum.im}}</ref>
[[File:Chthamalus southwardorum, 28866 Col., México imported from iNaturalist photo 366206710.jpg|thumb|''[[Chthamalus southwardorum]]'', a barnacle discovered in 2007 and named in Southward's honour "for his extensive contribution to the knowledge of the chthamalids"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pitombo |first1=Fabio Bettini |last2=Burton |first2=Ron |date=August 21, 2018 |title=Systematics and biogeography of Tropical Eastern Pacific ''Chthamalus'' with descriptions of two new species (Cirripedia, Thoracica). Zootaxa 1574: 1–30 (2007) |url=https://www.mapress.com/zt/article/view/zootaxa.4461.2.12 |journal=Zootaxa |volume=4461 |issue=2 |page=300 |doi=10.11646/zootaxa.4461.2.12 |pmid=30314092 |issn=1175-5334|url-access=subscription }}</ref>]]
While working on the Isle of Man, he met Eve Judges and later married her. She was an expert on marine worms and life around [[hydrothermal vent]]s, and collaborated with him on his work over the next decades. Eve survived him, and died of stroke in 2023, at the age of 92.<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-04 |title=Obituary: Dr Eve Southward |url=https://www.mba.ac.uk/obituary-dr-eve-southward/ |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=[[Marine Biological Association]] |language=en-GB |archive-date=2026-03-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260315172025/https://www.mba.ac.uk/obituary-dr-eve-southward/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Alan Southward was quite deaf and learned to [[Lip reading|lip-read]] when he was young;<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /> his deafness also affected his sense of balance.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> However, this did give him virtual immunity to sea-sickness;<ref name="Times Obit" /> apparently, the only time he felt bothered by it was during a [[Beaufort scale|force-12]] wind storm.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> Southward eschewed sign language but was a "greatly proficient lip-reader", assisted by his wife, who took notes for him and accompanied him to meetings.<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /><ref name="Chris Fry" />

Southward  worked as the editor of ''[[Advances in Marine Biology]]'' for 20 years. Southward supported Soviet scientists publishing their work in English to reach a broader audience, and helped Russian biologists find funding after the Soviet Union collapsed.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> He also wrote for newspapers.<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /> He was an honorary fellow of the [[Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom|Marine Biological Association]] and served as vice-chairman of that organization's Devon and Cornwall branch.<ref name="Chris Fry" /> In 2006, he was made an honorary fellow of the [[Linnean Society of London|Linnaean Society]], and he also served as an honorary professor at the [[University of Liverpool]] and the Canadian [[University of Victoria]].<ref name="Steve Hawkins" />

Southward died on 27 October 2007 of a heart attack.<ref name="Times Obit" />

== Research and work ==
[[File:Chthamalus proteus, Patillas, Puerto Rico imported from iNaturalist photo 362685629.jpg|thumb|''[[Chthamalus proteus]],'' a barnacle first described in 1980 by Southward and his colleague Paul Dando.]]
Southward's work focused on the [[intertidal zone]] and its ecology,<ref name="Chris Fry" /> and he spent much of his working life in Plymouth studying the surrounding waters.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> Starting in 1953, he was employed at the [[Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom|Marine Biological Association]]'s laboratories there.<ref name="Chris Fry" /> Southward was also a "world expert on the taxonomy of barnacles",<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /> studied their [[biogeography]],<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> and wrote two books on the animals, in 1987 and 2008.<ref name="Times Obit" /> He studied the aftermath of the 1967 [[Torrey Canyon oil spill]] and found that the dispersants used were actually toxic themselves and had dire long-term effects on wildlife.<ref name="Chris Fry" /> Southward's work beginning in the 1950s centred on the relation between the biogeography of small marine organisms and "minor changes in environmental conditions". This work culminated in the publication of a 1971 paper in ''Nature'' by Southward, F. S. Russell, G. T. Bolach, and E. I. Butler titled ''Changes in Biological Conditions in the English Channel off Plymouth during the Last Half Century'', which identified the links between water and chemical conditions and plankton abundance.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Russell |first1=F. S. |last2=Southward |first2=A. J. |last3=Boalch |first3=G. T. |last4=Butler |first4=E. I. |title=Changes in Biological Conditions in the English Channel off Plymouth during the Last Half Century |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/234468a0 |journal=Nature |date=1971 |language=en |volume=234 |issue=5330 |pages=468–470 |doi=10.1038/234468a0 |bibcode=1971Natur.234..468R |issn=1476-4687 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=2024-05-10 |access-date=2026-03-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510030701/https://www.nature.com/articles/234468a0 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, in the 1970s, he and his wife worked on the biota of deep-sea hydrothermal vents, and the role of [[chemosynthetic]] bacteria in those [[Community (ecology)|communities]].<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /> During his retirement, his work focused increasingly on the ecosystems of hydrothermal vents. The [[University of Victoria]] offered him a position as adjunct professor to study them in the Pacific Ocean.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> He also had a life-long interest in [[Pogonophora (worm)|pogonophores]], a type of tube worm.<ref name="Paul R. Dando" /> Southward officially retired from the Marine Biological Association in 1987, when he was almost 60 years old, but continued to work in marine biology:<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /> for example, in 2005 he collaborated on a paper in ''Advances in Marine Biology'' titled "Long-term oceanographic and ecological research in the Western English Channel".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Southward |first1=Alan J |last2=Langmead |first2=Olivia |last3=Hardman-Mountford |first3=Nicholas J |last4=Aiken |first4=James |last5=Boalch |first5=Gerald T |last6=Dando |first6=Paul R |last7=Genner |first7=Martin J |last8=Joint |first8=Ian |last9=Kendall |first9=Michael A |last10=Halliday |first10=Nicholas C |last11=Harris |first11=Roger P |last12=Leaper |first12=Rebecca |last13=Mieszkowska |first13=Nova |last14=Pingree |first14=Robin D |last15=Richardson |first15=Anthony J |display-authors=1 |date=2005-01-01 |title=Long-term oceanographic and ecological research in the Western English Channel |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2881(04)47001-1 |journal=Advances in Marine Biology |volume=47 |pages=1–105 |doi=10.1016/s0065-2881(04)47001-1 |issn=2162-5875 |pmid=15596166|isbn=978-0-12-026148-2 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Publications ==
{{Wikispecies|Alan James Southward}}Southward contributed some 220 papers over his lifetime, as well as two books: 

* ''[[iarchive:lifeonseashore0000alan/page/n71/mode/2up|Life on the Seashore]]'' (1967)
* ''Barnacle Biology'' (1987)
* ''British Barnacles'' (2008)

''British Barnacles'' was completed a month before he died and published by the [[Linnean Society of London|Linnean Society]].<ref name="Steve Hawkins" /><ref name="Chris Fry" />
